title: How the Lock and Key Evolved
upload_title: How Locks Evolved 🔑 From a Wooden Bar to Your Phone #shorts #engineering

beats.text: Before locks, anyone could walk into your home.
People jammed doors with wooden bars, but only from inside. Leave, and your home was open.
Ancient Egyptians built a wooden lock. Hidden pins held the bolt, and only the right key could lift them.
But those keys were huge, and wood cracks.
The Romans switched to iron and bronze, with keys small enough to wear as a ring.
In 1784, Joseph Bramah offered a prize to anyone who could pick his lock. It took 67 years.
In the 1860s, Linus Yale Junior made the pin tumbler lock cheap. Most front doors still use it.
The right key lifts every pin to one line, so the cylinder turns.
Today, many doors open with a code, a card, or your phone.
Follow to see how everything evolved.
